osteoporosis.reason: Loaded spinal flexion and forward bending stress vertebrae.
osteoporosis.alternative: Use neutral spine core stabilizers and supine leg slides.

osteoporosis.reason: Inversion and end-range spinal loading can compress weak bones.
osteoporosis.alternative: Replace with gentle pelvic tilts in supine.

osteoporosis.reason: Rounded spine rolling applies repeated flexion stress.
osteoporosis.alternative: Choose supported knee folds or single-leg stretches.

osteoporosis.reason: Forward flexion with load increases vertebral compression risk.
osteoporosis.alternative: Try seated postural work with neutral spine extension.

osteoporosis.reason: High-load core lift in flexion and balance can strain the spine.
osteoporosis.alternative: Use modified supported sit-up progressions with a ball.

osteoporosis.reason: Inversion and loaded spinal articulation may compress fragile vertebrae.
osteoporosis.alternative: Choose gentle supine leg slides or pelvic tilts with neutral spine.

pregnancy.reason: Heavy abdominal flexion can stress the growing uterus and diastasis recti.
pregnancy.alternative: Move to side-lying or supported seated core work.

pregnancy.reason: Inversion and supine leg lift may be uncomfortable after mid-pregnancy.
pregnancy.alternative: Use gentle pelvic floor breathing in seated or side-lying.

pregnancy.reason: Full sit-up style lifting and balance can overwork the linea alba.
pregnancy.alternative: Focus on neutral spine posture and pelvic floor activation.

pregnancy.reason: Supported head and torso lift from supine can strain the belly and neck.
pregnancy.alternative: Use safe standing or side-lying core variations.

pregnancy.reason: Inversion and spinal compression are best avoided during pregnancy.
pregnancy.alternative: Choose side-lying stretches and gentle supported hip work.

low_back_pain.reason: Repetitive spinal flexion can aggravate a painful disc or posterior chain.
low_back_pain.alternative: Choose pelvic tilts and supported bridging with neutral spine.

low_back_pain.reason: Loaded rolling may flare low back symptoms.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use gentle seated or supine core stabilization exercises.

low_back_pain.reason: Rotation with spinal flexion can irritate a sensitive lumbar spine.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use hip-focused side-lying work and neutral spine rotation.

low_back_pain.reason: Inversion and lumbar extension can be too intense for many back conditions.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions and gentle hip lifts.

low_back_pain.reason: Spinal articulation with inversion can aggravate low back pain and neural tension.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use neutral pelvic stabilization exercises and gentle supine stretch work.

hypertension.reason: Inversion may raise blood pressure and should be avoided.
hypertension.alternative: Use seated or quadruped mobility with steady breathing.

hypertension.reason: High-effort inversion can stress the cardiovascular system.
hypertension.alternative: Choose neutral spine plank holds or seated leg work.

hypertension.reason: Breath-holding and rapid rotation may spike blood pressure.
hypertension.alternative: Use slow, controlled hip circles with relaxed breathing.

hypertension.reason: Balance inversions can feel too intense for heart concerns.
hypertension.alternative: Stay on the mat with core stability and leg lifts.

hypertension.reason: Inversion and spinal compression can elevate blood pressure in sensitive individuals.
hypertension.alternative: Choose low-lying core stabilization and gentle standing mobility.

knee_issues.reason: Deep hip lift can load knees and aggravate joint pain.
knee_issues.alternative: Use gentle pelvic tilts and supported glute bridges.

knee_issues.reason: Plank-based leg lifts place pressure on the knees and hips.
knee_issues.alternative: Work in quadruped with lifted legs or side-lying leg lifts.

knee_issues.reason: Prone leg extensions can irritate knee or hamstring tension.
knee_issues.alternative: Use seated or side-lying single-leg moves with reduced range.

knee_issues.reason: Repeated knee flexion may strain arthritic joints.
knee_issues.alternative: Choose static leg holds or gentle marching in supine.

knee_issues.reason: Reformer leg pressing can place continuous load through sensitive knees.
knee_issues.alternative: Use seated or supported legwork with small range and lighter resistance.

hip_issues.reason: Large hip circles can aggravate painful or unstable hips.
hip_issues.alternative: Use smaller leg circles or hip hinges with support.

hip_issues.reason: Extreme hip range in supine can irritate hip joints.
hip_issues.alternative: Keep legs lower and work with smaller controlled lifts.

hip_issues.reason: Wide open leg balance places strain on the hip capsule.
hip_issues.alternative: Use seated adductor and abductor control work.

hip_issues.reason: Rotational hip motion may be painful if the joint is inflamed.
hip_issues.alternative: Choose gentle supported hip pumps in supine.

hip_issues.reason: Repeated leg pressing can irritate sensitive hips due to loaded flexion and extension.
hip_issues.alternative: Work with small range and lighter resistance, or choose supine leg slides.

neck_shoulder.reason: Sustained lifted head and neck can aggravate cervical tension.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Keep the head supported while maintaining core breath.

neck_shoulder.reason: Unsupported head lift increases neck strain and shoulder tension.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use chin-tucks and gentle supported rolling in a neutral neck.

neck_shoulder.reason: Head lift with balance can load neck and shoulder stabilizers.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use seated supported core work and avoid full V position.

neck_shoulder.reason: Prone back extension stresses the neck and upper shoulders.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use gentle prone lifts with hands under shoulders for support.

neck_shoulder.reason: Loading the shoulders over the bar can aggravate shoulder instability or neck tension.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use gentle supported back extension with lower resistance.

neck_shoulder.reason: Reformer shoulder loading under an inverted spine can stress tight neck/shoulder areas.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Choose supported prone back extension or supine spine mobilization without inversion.

recent_surgery.reason: Loaded spinal flexion is often too aggressive after surgery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Focus on gentle breathing, pelvic floor, and posture support.

recent_surgery.reason: Inversion and deep articulation can be unsafe during recovery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Choose supported movements and follow professional clearance.

recent_surgery.reason: Twisting with load may stress healing tissues.
recent_surgery.alternative: Use neutral spine rotation from seated or standing positions.

recent_surgery.reason: Lateral flexion can be uncomfortable after surgery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Keep movements gentle and avoid end-range bending.

recent_surgery.reason: Inversion and deep spinal articulation are usually contraindicated after recent surgery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Use gentle supine pelvic tilts and supported spine mobilization.

arthritis.reason: Repetitive flexion may aggravate stiff joints.
arthritis.alternative: Use small spinal articulations and neutral core work.

arthritis.reason: Rotation with forward flexion can irritate arthritic joints.
arthritis.alternative: Use seated side-lying rotation with support.

arthritis.reason: Inverted hip circles may be too intense for sensitive joints.
arthritis.alternative: Choose simple hip circles with reduced range.

arthritis.reason: Rolling can feel harsh on arthritic spine or hips.
arthritis.alternative: Use supported core strengthening without dynamic rolling.

arthritis.reason: Reformer leg press work can aggravate arthritic knee or hip joints without careful load management.
arthritis.alternative: Use lighter resistance and focus on small controlled range.

arthritis.reason: Inversion and spinal compression may be uncomfortable for arthritic joints.
arthritis.alternative: Choose gentle spine mobilization without large range or inversion.

scoliosis.reason: Large spinal flexion can accentuate the curve if not controlled.
scoliosis.alternative: Use supported roll-downs with a neutral pelvis and asymmetry awareness.

scoliosis.reason: Rotation through the spine may create uneven loading in a curved spine.
scoliosis.alternative: Do gentle seated side stretches with equal attention to both sides.

scoliosis.reason: Deep asymmetric side flexion can strain a scoliotic curve.
scoliosis.alternative: Work with small side bends and keep the ribs long.

pelvic_floor_dysfunction.reason: Strong abdominal pumping and breath coordination may increase pelvic floor pressure.
pelvic_floor_dysfunction.alternative: Keep the head supported and focus on gentle pelvic floor engagement.

pelvic_floor_dysfunction.reason: Repeated hip flexion and lower abdominal engagement can irritate a weak pelvic floor.
pelvic_floor_dysfunction.alternative: Perform supported knee folds or modified marching with neutral pelvis.

pelvic_floor_dysfunction.reason: Full sit-up movement loads the pelvic floor and linea alba.
pelvic_floor_dysfunction.alternative: Use supported seated core work and avoid full V position.

diastasis_recti.reason: Strong abdominal pumping can widen the separation and increase intra-abdominal pressure.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Use supported core work with the head down and focus on transverse abdominis engagement.

diastasis_recti.reason: Loaded spinal flexion places stress on the linea alba.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Practice pelvic tilts and supported roll-downs with a neutral spine.

diastasis_recti.reason: Full V-position and abdominal lift can overstress separated abdominal muscles.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Use modified seated core work with bent knees and low lift.

diastasis_recti.reason: Combined lower ab extension and arm reach may increase pressure through the midline.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Choose heel slides and single-leg supports with minimal abdominal strain.

shoulder_instability.reason: Heavy shoulder loading over the bar may aggravate instability or impingement.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Use supported back extension with lighter resistance and stable shoulder placement.

shoulder_instability.reason: Prone extension can place excessive demand on the neck and shoulder stabilizers.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Choose gentle prone lifting with hands under shoulders for support.

shoulder_instability.reason: Repeated alternating arm lifts can overwork unstable shoulder joints.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Use lower range arm extension with more emphasis on scapular stability.

shoulder_instability.reason: Shoulder-supported bridge positions may increase discomfort if the shoulders are unstable.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Keep the upper body relaxed and work with lower bridge variations or supine glute engagement.

bursitis.reason: Large hip circles can irritate inflamed bursae around the hip or pelvis.
bursitis.alternative: Use smaller, slower leg circles with a supported pelvis.

bursitis.reason: Repetitive hip rotation may aggravate bursitis in the hip joint.
bursitis.alternative: Choose gentle supported hip pumps in a neutral range.

bursitis.reason: Prone back extension can compress already tender shoulder bursae.
bursitis.alternative: Work with supported chest lifts and avoid aggressive upper back extension.

bursitis.reason: Extended upper-body reach and loaded carriage movement may stress sensitive shoulder tissues.
bursitis.alternative: Use lighter springs and smaller arm movements while keeping the shoulders stable.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Inversion can trigger dizziness and disorientation.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Choose gentle supine pelvic tilts or seated mobility instead.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Rapid spinal rotation with legs overhead can disrupt balance.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Use slow hip circles with the head supported and eyes fixed.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Inversion and sudden balance challenge may worsen vertigo.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Stay on the mat with supported bridge progressions and slow movement.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Advanced inversions and balancing can provoke lightheadedness.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Focus on floor-based core stability and steady breath.

postpartum.reason: Loaded spinal flexion and abdominal lifting can stress a recovering postpartum core.
postpartum.alternative: Use supported pelvic tilts and gentle seated core reconnection work.

postpartum.reason: Full V-style lifting can overload the healing linea alba and pelvic floor.
postpartum.alternative: Practice supported seated core lifts with bent knees and gentle breath.

postpartum.reason: Strong abdominal extension and reach may overpressure a recovering midline.
postpartum.alternative: Choose heel slides and single-leg supports with minimal abdominal strain.

balance_issues.reason: Advanced balance work increases fall risk and instability.
balance_issues.alternative: Focus on grounded floor-based stability and slow core control.

balance_issues.reason: Inversion and high balance demand can be too challenging for unstable clients.
balance_issues.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions and low-level hip lifts.

balance_issues.reason: Legs overhead inversion can challenge balance and spatial orientation.
balance_issues.alternative: Choose seated or supine core mobility without inversion.

joint_replacement.reason: Reformer leg pressing can place too much load on a replaced knee or hip.
joint_replacement.alternative: Use lighter springs, smaller range of motion, or seated leg support.

joint_replacement.reason: Loaded knee flexion and hip movement can strain a replaced joint.
joint_replacement.alternative: Choose supported knee lifts with minimal range and controlled alignment.

joint_replacement.reason: Large hip circles may aggravate a replaced hip joint.
joint_replacement.alternative: Use smaller supported leg circles or isometric hip stability work.

foot_ankle_issues.reason: Reformer footbar work places repeated load through the ankles and forefoot.
foot_ankle_issues.alternative: Use lighter resistance and keep the feet flat with minimal plantarflexion.

foot_ankle_issues.reason: Weight-bearing through the feet and ankles can aggravate sensitive joints.
foot_ankle_issues.alternative: Choose seated or supported hamstring stretches without heavy foot load.

foot_ankle_issues.reason: Rapid lower-leg movement and pointed foot positions can irritate ankle or foot pain.
foot_ankle_issues.alternative: Use slower supine leg circles with a neutral foot position.

chronic_fatigue.reason: High-repetition breath and core work can worsen fatigue if pacing is too aggressive.
chronic_fatigue.alternative: Use shorter sets, gentler breath work, and allow rest breaks.

chronic_fatigue.reason: Sustained prone arm and leg lifts can be too demanding for low-energy clients.
chronic_fatigue.alternative: Choose single-limb lifts with frequent recovery pauses.

chronic_fatigue.reason: Extended plank-based leg lifts may overtax a fatigued body.
chronic_fatigue.alternative: Use supported quadruped or supine core exercises with less sustained load.

diabetes.reason: High-resistance leg work can be challenging if circulation or neuropathy is present.
diabetes.alternative: Use lighter springs and focus on smooth, controlled carriage movement.

diabetes.reason: Prolonged prone effort may fatigue the shoulders and legs quickly.
diabetes.alternative: Choose shorter duration posterior chain work with frequent rest.

diabetes.reason: Rapid alternating lower body movement can be uncomfortable if sensation is reduced.
diabetes.alternative: Use slower leg rhythms and keep the pelvis stable.

weight_concerns.reason: High core and balance demand can be difficult under added body weight.
weight_concerns.alternative: Use supported core lifts with bent knees and a lower center of gravity.

weight_concerns.reason: Inversion and rapid leg lifting may increase strain on the lower back and hips.
weight_concerns.alternative: Choose supported bridges and slower hip lifts with a neutral spine.

weight_concerns.reason: Dynamic rolling balance can be unstable and overly demanding on the joints.
weight_concerns.alternative: Focus on controlled seated or supine core work with stable foot contact.

weight_concerns.reason: Advanced balance and leg extension demand can tax joint control and stability.
weight_concerns.alternative: Use grounded stability exercises with both feet on the mat and small range movements.

respiratory.reason: Inversions and upper-body compression can make breathing difficult for people with asthma.
respiratory.alternative: Use supported chest lifts and avoid chest-compressive or breath-holding positions.

respiratory.reason: Legs-overhead position and spinal flexion can restrict the rib cage and challenge breathing.
respiratory.alternative: Choose gentle supine core work with the head and chest supported.

respiratory.reason: Rapid breath cycling and core intensity may trigger wheezing or breathlessness.
respiratory.alternative: Practice slower breath-based abdominal work with frequent rest and open chest posture.
